docs.title: Zoha
docs.text: Zoha is a personal assistant you talk to. She opens apps, finds files, answers questions and builds web pages, and she asks before doing anything that matters.

docs.title: What makes her different
docs.text:
• Voice first. Say "Zoha, open Spotify" or type it. Both work.
  • Builds checked web pages. Every page she writes is linted and fixed before she shows it.
  • Asks first. Shutdown, restart, sleep and website changes need a clear yes.
  • Your brain, your choice. Gemini, any OpenAI-compatible API, or a local model through Ollama.
  • Open source. Apache-2.0. Add plugins and skills as plain files.

Zoha supports Windows first. Ports to macOS and Linux are welcome.

Install Zoha{ .md-button }

docs.title: Choosing a brain
docs.text:
Zoha doesn't ship a model. Pick one in setup_wizard.py, or edit .env:

Brain Set Also set Gemini LLM_PROVIDER=gemini GEMINI_API_KEY, GEMINI_MODEL Any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenRouter, OpenAI, ...) LLM_PROVIDER=openai LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL Local model (Ollama) LLM_PROVIDER=local LOCAL_LLM_URL, LOCAL_LLM_MODEL (for example qwen3.5:4b)

LLM_FALLBACK names a second brain to switch to when the first runs out of quota or is offline (none turns it off). Simple commands such as open, volume and time are also handled by Zoha's built-in parser before any model is called.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Does Zoha work on macOS or Linux? Not yet. She is Windows first. Ports are welcome; see CONTRIBUTING.

Is my voice sent anywhere? Speech recognition runs on your computer. Only the text of your request goes to the brain you chose.

Can she shut down my PC by accident? No. Shutdown, restart and sleep always ask first and only act after your next message is a clear yes.

How do I add a feature? Drop a Python file in plugins/ or a Markdown file in skills/.

Where are my settings? In .env. Run python setup_wizard.py to change them.

docs.title: Talk a website into existence
docs.text:
Say "Zoha, make a website for my bakery". If you give no details she asks one short question at a time (name, city, what you sell, colours), builds the page, tests it and opens it. Edit it by talking ("make the heading bigger", "add a menu section"). Then say "publish it".

Publishing needs a free Netlify personal access token in .env as NETLIFY_TOKEN. Zoha asks first and only publishes after a clear yes. Only the page and its own _files / _photos folders are uploaded. The token is never logged or spoken. The same page keeps the same address when you publish it again.

docs.title: Business desk (plugin)
docs.text: plugins/business_desk.py, for small businesses: - "Make a quotation for Mr Shah: cabinets 2 at 45000, hob 1 at 12k, 18 percent GST" makes a printable quotation in Documents/Zoha Quotes (use Print to save a PDF). Amounts use lakh/crore grouping. - "Mr Shah owes 30000, due the 5th", "who hasn't paid?", "he paid" keep a simple list in data/business.json on your computer. - "Write a follow-up for Mr Shah" (English or Hinglish) only drafts a message to copy. Zoha never sends anything for you.

docs.title: Routines (teach by showing)
docs.text: "Learn this as work mode", then ask for your steps as usual (open your editor, set the volume, play music), then say "that's it". Later: "start work mode". Zoha records the safe tool actions you ask for, not mouse clicks. She never records shutdown, restart, sleep, website changes, publishing, file writing, browser actions or other routines, and tells you what she left out.

docs.title: Chat widget for a business website
docs.text:
A small chat and call-back box that answers only from the facts you give it.

python -m zoha.widget_server init     # creates widget_config.json: fill in the business and the site's address
python -m zoha.widget_server serve

Paste the printed <script> tag into the website. It is public, so it is limited: only the origins in allowed_origins may use it, 12 messages a minute per visitor, a daily reply cap, short messages and answers, and it never invents prices. Call-back requests are saved to data/widget_leads.jsonl. Put it behind HTTPS (a small server or a tunnel) before using it on a real site. It uses the brain set in .env, so a cloud model costs money per reply; the cap is there to limit that.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
You need Windows 10 or 11 and Python 3.12 or newer.

git clone https://github.com/zhessor/zoha.git
cd zoha
.\setup.ps1

setup.ps1 creates a virtual environment, installs the packages, offers the GPU extras if you have an NVIDIA card, and starts the setup wizard. The wizard asks your name, city and which brain to use, then writes .env.

Start the desktop app:

.\venv\Scripts\python.exe gui.py

Text-only mode: python main.py --text.

docs.title: Zoha plugins
docs.text:
Every .py file in this folder is loaded when Zoha starts. Use it to give Zoha new tools without touching the core code.

from zoha.tools import tool

@tool("tool_name", "When the model should use it (one clear sentence).", "Label shown in the app", "⚡",
      city=("string", "What this argument is", True))   # (type, description, required[, enum])
def tool_name(city: str) -> str:
    return "Short plain-text result for the model to summarise"

Rules for good plugins: - One job per tool, with a description that says when to use it. - Return short text. The model reads it and answers in its own words. - Never log or return secrets. Read keys from .env with os.getenv. - Ask before anything that can't be undone (sending, paying, deleting). Return a summary and let the user confirm, the way zoha/site_plugin.py does. - Files starting with _ are ignored, which is handy for drafts.

See coin_and_dice.py for a working example. Pull requests that add plugins are welcome.

docs.title: Site Agent API (for the website/CMS plugin)
docs.text: Zoha's site_* tools talk to your website through a small JSON API. Build these endpoints on your site (any stack), set SITE_API_URL, SITE_API_KEY and SITE_NAME in .env, and Zoha can read your content, enquiries and analytics and propose changes.

docs.title: Safety model (keep it when you implement this)
docs.text:
1. Zoha can never change the site directly. POST /changes only creates a proposal with a human-readable summary.
  2. Zoha reads the summary out loud. Only when the user's very next words are a clear "yes" does it call POST /changes/{id}/apply. Anything else cancels it (POST /changes/{id}/cancel).
  3. A proposal must expire on the server after 5 minutes and be applicable once (return 410 when expired).
  4. Auth: Authorization: Bearer <SITE_API_KEY>. Zoha never logs, speaks or puts the key in URLs. Rotate it if leaked.

docs.title: Endpoints (all JSON, relative to SITE_API_URL)
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose GET /describe What content types exist and their editable fields, so the model knows what it can change GET /read?type=&q=&id= Read items of a type (pricing, testimonials, posts…), optionally filtered GET /enquiries?limit=5 Latest contact-form enquiries and the unread count POST /enquiries/{id}/status { "status": "archived" } and similar POST /enquiries/{id}/reply { "body": "..." } → a reply draft with an id and summary POST /replies/{id}/apply Send that draft (only after the user's yes) GET /analytics?range=7d Visitors and KPIs vs the previous period, top pages and sources POST /changes { type, action: create/update/delete, id?, fields, reason } → proposal { id, summary, expiresAt } POST /changes/{id}/apply Apply a proposal (once, within 5 minutes) POST /changes/{id}/cancel Drop a proposal GET /changes?limit=10 History of changes with status POST /undo { "changeId": "..." } → a proposal that reverses it (same confirm flow)

Errors: return { "error": "plain sentence" } with a normal HTTP status. Zoha reads the sentence to the user.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is a Markdown file in skills/ that tells Zoha how you want something done (for example, how to write an email or what a good landing page includes). It is plain text and never runs code.

---
name: email
description: Write short, polite emails
---

# Steps
...

Install one from a link:

python -m zoha.skill_install install https://github.com/someone/repo/blob/main/skills/report.md
python -m zoha.skill_install list

The file must have a name and description header and be under 64 KB. An existing skill is never replaced unless you add --force.
